H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper has top-level Mode 1-4 microgrid modes, while Mode 1 and Mode 2/3 each contain BESS three-stage charging submodes: constant power, constant voltage, and floating.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions use SOC hysteresis thresholds, an OR fault guard such as SOC > GenSOC_ub OR genset protection activated, and internal comparisons such as df2 > df1.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Per-mode actions include BESS V/f regulation, power dispatch, PV freq-watt curtailment, generator synchronization, load shedding, and complete shutdown/disconnection.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: A generator overcurrent/undercurrent trip sends Mode 2 or Mode 3 back to Mode 1; Mode 4 is a low-SOC shutdown path from Mode 3.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Mode duties are in Table I, transition guards are in Fig. 6/Section III.C, and synchronization/charging actions are explained in separate Section III.B prose.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as genset protection, resynchronization strategy, grid-forming, grid-feeding, and freq-watt curtailment require domain decoding beyond the flat state list.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The explicit mode table does not co-locate all actions; generator synchronization and frequency-based PV curtailment are described later in narrative control sections.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The state machine includes SOC > GenSOC_ub OR genset protection activated, and the BESS controller compares computed quantities such as df2 > df1.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Mode 1 has parent behavior such as BESS voltage/frequency regulation while its internal charging controller switches among constant-power, constant-voltage, and floating modes.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The fault transition is specified only from Mode 2 or Mode 3 to Mode 1, not as an explicit from-any-state global recovery rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: Although there are nested control modes, the paper does not specify a deep composite-state init or pseudo-state routing chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are composed/computed guards such as OR protection and df2 > df1, but not three or more clearly arithmetic-and-boolean transition guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Mode-level continuous behavior such as BESS V/f regulation, power dispatch, and freq-watt curtailment could be declared once as during behavior; generator trip also cuts across Mode 2 and Mode 3.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The outputs are mostly concrete control actions on BESS, PV, generator, relays, loads, and frequency/power references, not abstract notifications or channel-agnostic side effects.

key_nl_quotes: Battery SOC is the main trigger for state transitions.
Mode 4 represents the mode where all the units are shut down and disconnected.
one_line_pitch: This is a hard stress test because a four-mode SOC-hysteresis supervisor is intertwined with nested battery charging modes, nontrivial continuous control actions, and generator-trip recovery.
rationale: The sample has meaningful hierarchy, strong guard structure, rich per-mode actions, and an explicit fault-driven recovery path. Its state names, guards, and actions are spread across the operation table, state-machine figure, smooth-transition section, and BESS control sections, which directly stresses baseline context retention. It is not excluded: the paper provides enough concrete modes, guards, actions, and recovery semantics to construct a reference EFSM.
